title: Bounded termwise-flat stalk complex for local counit localization
statement: Under the affine open presentation hypothesis, for arbitrary qcqs p, relatively flat quasi-coherent M, g and a, the stalk ring R at g(a) admits a bounded-above termwise-flat cochain complex P.

proof.text: Choose HomologicalComplex.zero over the base stalk ring and use zero as an upper bound. Every component is a zero object, hence its underlying module is subsingleton by ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero. Mathlib makes a subsingleton module free (Module.Free.of_subsingleton), and a free module flat (Module.Flat.of_free). Thus the zero complex has the required boundedness and termwise flatness. No affine-presentation or relative-flatness hypothesis is needed for this existential conclusion.

mathlib_searches.query: bounded flat stalk complex derived scalar extension

lean.statement:
theorem standardSingleFlatCounit_localization_data
    (h_affine : ∀ {Y₀ B₀ A₀ : Scheme.{u}} (p₀ : Y₀ ⟶ B₀)
      [QuasiCompact p₀] [QuasiSeparated p₀] [IsAffine B₀] [IsAffine A₀]
      (g₀ : A₀ ⟶ B₀), StandardSingleFlatCounitOnOpen p₀ g₀ ⊤)
    {Y B A : Scheme.{u}} (p : Y ⟶ B) [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
    (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] (hM : M.IsFlatOver p) (g : A ⟶ B) (a : A) :
    letI := fun X : Scheme.{u} ↦ HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    let R := B.presheaf.stalk (g a)
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ),
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (P.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Flat R (P.X i))
